title: How do we find the area of a path around a park?
description: A path is laid around a rectangular park, and the park and the path together make a bigger rectangle. The area of the park is taken away from the area of the bigger rectangle, and the answer is checked by cutting the path into four strips.
teaching_notes: One idea: the area of the path is the area of the bigger rectangle take away the area of the park. Watch for children who add the two areas or measure only the length of the path.

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 2)
video_script.why: The child finds the area of a region that is not a rectangle by working with two rectangles whose areas come from length times width.
video_script.substitution: Find the area of the bigger rectangle and of the park, take one away from the other, and check with the four strips of the path.
video_script.anchor: the rectangular park EFGH with a shaded path laid around it inside the rectangle ABCD, from the book
video_script.payoff_line: the area of the path is one hundred twenty square metres

final_answer.value: Area of path = area of ABCD − area of EFGH = 120 m² for the chosen values

hold_back: the area of the path is 120 m²
never_show: the area of the path, before the answer beat
maths_rules: chosen values: outer rectangle ABCD 20 m by 14 m, park EFGH 16 m by 10 m
area of ABCD = 20 × 14 = 280 m²; area of EFGH = 16 × 10 = 160 m²
area of path = 280 − 160 = 120 m²; formula: area of ABCD − area of EFGH
moving ABCD with the park kept inside: both rectangles keep their sizes, so the path area stays 120 m²
check: path 2 m wide on every side ((20 − 16) ÷ 2 = 2 and (14 − 10) ÷ 2 = 2); two strips 20 × 2 = 40 each, two strips 10 × 2 = 20 each; 2 × 40 + 2 × 20 = 80 + 40 = 120 m²
video_script.design: One idea: path area is the outer rectangle take away the park. The park, the path and the bigger rectangle stay on stage. The values are chosen, as the book asks. The formula, the move of the bigger rectangle, and the four strips (a path of equal width, used as the check) are all shown.
open_questions: The book figure is not in the extracted text, so the picture is drawn from the question; the chosen values 20 m by 14 m and 16 m by 10 m are the worklist's, as the book asks the child to choose values.
